title: Do full bond-distance tables decide every three-parent join at widths 21 through 26?
claim: Either certify the first opposing full-table isometry in the new interval or prove by exhaustive calculation that all reachable presentations in the six widths agree on their marked triple verdicts. Treat the unrestricted inverse as a separate theorem.
standard_statement: Decide whether complete pairwise minimum cocircuit cardinalities of a serial binary incidence family determine its unordered three-coordinate extension predicate, for orders 21 through 26 inclusive.
prior_work: The same finite predicate has been checked through order 20 and in an individual 32-coordinate example.
completion_gate: A certified first opposing pair, or exhaustive authority for every width 21 through 26 inclusive.
source_contribution: Only the current anonymous bond-distance matrix, a proposed triple and the growth law are supplied.

validation.status: Passed by separate algorithms in the same task

conclusion: Every renaming preserving the full bond-distance table between reachable realizations in this interval preserves three-parent legality. Together with the lower widths this gives a first possible collision at width 27. The unrestricted all-size problem remains open.
evidence_class: Computer-assisted finite theorem for six complete widths and restricted all-size structural lemmas.
remaining_scientific_question: Can an arbitrary marked full-table isometry flip a three-parent verdict at width 27 or greater? If so, does a three-way bond reading suffice at every width?
failure_conditions: A missing reachable type, a duplicate ordinary type, or a full-table isometry in this interval with different triple verdicts would invalidate the interval claim.
A reachable rival violating a restricted all-size statement with all its hypotheses would invalidate that structural lemma.
